title: Dragnet
paragraphs: NBC police procedural based on actual LAPD cases and developed around documentary realism.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: Joe Friday / Ben Romero new-production era (June 3, 1949 to December 13, 1951) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], Partner-transition era (December 27, 1951 to September 14, 1952) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], Joe Friday / Frank Smith new-production era (September 21, 1952 to September 20, 1955) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], and NBC rerun era (September 27, 1955 to February 26, 1957) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include [[person|jack-webb|Jack Webb]] (performer and producer), Ben Alexander (performer and writer), George Fenneman (announcer and commercial spokesman), Barton Yarborough (performer), Walter Schumann (music, conductor, and announcer), Hal Gibney (announcer and host), and John Robinson (writer).

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]], and [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]].

The stories often return to robbery and burglary, homicide investigation, juvenile crime and welfare, domestic and family crisis, missing persons and kidnapping, and police procedure and investigation.
The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Postwar urban policing and procedural realism, Police technical cooperation in mass-media drama, and Radio-to-television transition.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|escape|Escape]], [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]], [[show|broadway-is-my-beat|Broadway Is My Beat]], and [[show|the-whistler|The Whistler]].
